geometry_notes: Axis frame used below: s_axis along bearing 63 deg (u=(0.889,0.458)) and t_axis across (+t = NW), origin art (865.8,236.2) as in bld_qnc.py. Lidar (unclipped nDSM) gives: BAR = the big 4-5 storey block, s_axis -33..+44, t 10..37 (77 x 27 m), roof 25.5-27 m on most of it, 19.5-21 m along a 3 m strip at its NW edge for s_axis -6..+34 (east half of W0) and over its NE end s_axis 34..44 (the link block over W14/W15); CUBE s_axis +4..+48, t -20..+8 (about 44 x 28 m, not a cube), roof 33-34.5 m, plant to 39 m; PODIUM s_axis -21..+4, t -26..+10, 11.2 m, green roof; LOW SE BLOCK along W9, t -32..-20, 7.5-10.5 m, green roof strip with a deck terrace; WEST WING s_axis -47.5..-38, 5.3 m, green roof + terrace. So the 'striped box' of the ArchDaily photos is not a separate 26 m bar: it is the whole BAR block, whose SW end (above the west wing) and SE face (above the entrance and podium) carry the stripes. Because several important faces are upper faces not on any ground wall, they are given below as pseudo-walls U0-U6 with explicit art ends (same a->b convention, building on the left). Their ends are from lidar/ortho and good to about 2-3 m; lidar looked shifted about +2-3 m in s_axis relative to walls.json.
